source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Selectively slowing the heart rate through action on the sinoatrial node, without the blood pressure-lowering effects of a beta-blocker","B":"Blocking beta receptors directly throughout the body, working in essentially the same way a traditional beta-blocker medication would function","C":"Increasing the client's resting heart rate significantly as its primary intended pharmacologic effect on the sinoatrial node","D":"Having fairly little measurable effect on the client's heart rate at all once the medication has actually been started and titrated"}}
source_row.rationale: Ivabradine selectively slows heart rate through action on the sinoatrial node's pacemaker current, without the blood pressure-lowering effects of a beta-blocker, making it useful for heart failure clients with persistently elevated heart rate despite maximally tolerated beta-blocker therapy.
source_row.source_detail: Mechanism of Action Distinct from Beta-Blockers
